content: 1. Complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) often fulfills a demand that conventional medicine does not address or expands the conceptual frameworks of medical practice. (Ernst et al., British General Practitioner, 1995; 45:506) 2. Evidence-based complementary and alternative medicine is a growing field that seeks to integrate scientific validation into non-conventional therapies. 3. The Committee on Economic, Social, and Cultural Rights emphasized the right to the highest attainable standard of health in General Comment No. 14 (2000), highlighting the importance of access to diverse medical practices. 4. The Department of AYUSH (Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy) in India promotes traditional and alternative medical systems. 5. Ernst E. discussed the challenges in conducting research on complementary and alternative medicine in the Medical Journal of Australia, 2003; 179(6):279-80. (PMID 12964907) 6. Patients often turn to CAM for various reasons, including dissatisfaction with conventional treatments or a desire for holistic approaches. (Astin JA, JAMA, 1998; 279(19):1548-1553) 7. Trends in the use of alternative medicine in the United States from 1990 to 1997 were analyzed by Eisenberg DM et al., showing a significant increase in its popularity. (JAMA, 1998; 280:1569-1575, PMID 9820257) 8. The House of Lords report on CAM provided a comprehensive review of its status and integration into healthcare systems. 9. The University of Arizona has established a position on alternative medicine, emphasizing its role in integrative healthcare. 10. Wetzel MS, Eisenberg DM, and Kaptchuk TJ examined the inclusion of CAM courses in U.S. medical school curricula. (JAMA, 1998; 280(9):784-787, PMID 9729989) 11. Saxon DW et al. reviewed the status of CAM in osteopathic medical school curricula, highlighting its growing presence. (J Am Osteopath Assoc, 2004; 104(3):121-6, PMID 15083987) 12. Fenton MV and Morris DL explored the integration of holistic nursing practices and CAM modalities into nursing school curricula. (Altern Ther Health Med, 2003; 9(4):62-7) 13. Vickers A. critically analyzed alternative cancer cures, questioning whether they are unproven or disproven. (CA Cancer J Clin, 2004; 54:110-118) 14. Michalsen A et al. demonstrated that thermal hydrotherapy improves quality of life and hemodynamic function in patients with chronic heart failure. (Am Heart J, 2003; 146(4):E11, PMID 14564334) 15. Gonsalkorale WM et al. reported long-term benefits of hypnotherapy for irritable bowel syndrome. (Gut, 2003; 52(11):1623-9, PMID 14570733) 16. Berga SL et al. showed that cognitive behavioral therapy can restore ovarian activity in women with functional hypothalamic amenorrhea. (Fertility and Sterility, 2003; 80(4):976-981) 17. Kleijnen J et al. reviewed clinical trials of homeopathy, raising questions about its efficacy. (BMJ, 1991; 302:316-23, PMID 1825800) 18. Linde K et al. conducted a meta-analysis of placebo-controlled trials to determine whether the clinical effects of homeopathy are placebo effects. (Lancet, 1997; 350:834-43, PMID 9310601) 19. Snyderman R and Weil AT advocated for integrative medicine, emphasizing a return to the roots of holistic care. (Arch Intern Med, 2002; 162:395-397) 20. Hoffer LJ discussed the challenges of evaluating alternative cancer therapies, emphasizing the need for both proof and plausibility. (CMAJ, 2001; 164(3):351-3, PMID 11232135) 21. Larkin M raised concerns about authorship ethics in medical journals, particularly regarding honorary and ghost authors. (Lancet, 1999; 354:136) 22. Flanagin A et al. examined the prevalence of articles with honorary and ghost authors in peer-reviewed medical journals. (JAMA, 1998; 280(3):222-4) 23. James Alcock PhD explored the psychology of belief in alternative medicine, providing insights into why individuals may favor these practices. (The Scientific Review of Alternative Medicine, Fall/Winter 1999) 24. Ganzera M et al. developed and validated an HPLC/UV/MS method for detecting preservatives in grapefruit seed extract. (J Agric Food Chem, 2006; 54(11):3768-72) 25. Mahoney N identified benzethonium chloride in commercial grapefruit seed extracts, raising concerns about product purity. (J Agric Food Chem, 2001; 49(7):3316-20)
